subject.title: fix(reply): strip leaked current-message scaffolding and (no output) placeholders

question: Should OpenClaw accept this shared sanitizer/normalizer behavior as the cross-channel delivery contract once checks are clean or triaged?
rationale: The patch is a plausible and focused bug fix, but it changes the common path that decides whether reply text is stripped, skipped, or delivered across channels.

options.title: Accept Shared Delivery Semantics
options.body: Merge after the failing broad CI shards are rerun or explicitly triaged, keeping this as the common sanitizer/normalizer fix.

options.title: Request Live Telegram Proof
options.body: Ask for a short Telegram Desktop proof before merge if maintainers want transport-visible confirmation beyond production-function terminal output.

options.title: Pause For Narrower Semantics
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want marker stripping scoped differently or owned by a different delivery layer.

recommendation.title: Accept Shared Delivery Semantics
recommendation.body: Merge after the failing broad CI shards are rerun or explicitly triaged, keeping this as the common sanitizer/normalizer fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent history on the shared reply helper and dispatcher boundary that this PR changes.
